name: Light Up the Stage
oracle_text:
Spectacle {R} (You may cast this spell for its spectacle cost rather than its mana cost if an opponent lost life this turn.)
Exile the top two cards of your library. Until the end of your next turn, you may play those cards.
blocked_sentences: Until the end of your next turn, you may play those cards.

needs.what: an impulse-exile permission whose clock runs to the end of the granting player's NEXT turn instead of the current one. Concretely: replace the single `playable_turn: int` on GameObject (src/automtg/engine/objects.py:450) with a permission that also records its duration -- e.g. a `playable_until_next_turn: bool` alongside it, or a `playable_expires_after` marker the turn boundary clears -- and have every reader honour it: legality._playable_zones (src/automtg/engine/legality.py:325-336), the exile-permission filter at src/automtg/engine/legality.py:471, the any-type relaxation at src/automtg/engine/legality.py:1171 and src/automtg/engine/game.py:383, and the group cap at src/automtg/engine/game.py:547. Then surface it on the card side as a duration on `exile`'s `playable_this_turn` (a `playable: "until_your_next_turn"` form, or a sibling `playable_until_next_turn` flag) and the same on `grant_playable`, so the two impulse families -- "you may play that card this turn" and "until the end of your next turn, you may play those cards" -- stay one op with two clocks.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The permission the engine has is hard-wired to a single turn. `exile` with `playable_this_turn` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_board.py:267,293-294) and `grant_playable` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_cards.py:132-165) both write `obj.playable_turn = ctx.state.turn`, and every consumer gates on the equality `playable_turn == state.turn`, so the offer vanishes at the turn boundary -- a card written with `playable_this_turn` would let the player use the two exiled cards only on the turn Light Up the Stage resolved, which is strictly narrower than printed and is exactly the approximation the brief forbids. `play_exiled` is a different card entirely: it casts immediately and for free, while this line is a deferred permission at the printed price. `delay`/`delayed_trigger` cannot re-grant it either -- there is no way to re-select the two specific exiled cards from a later resolution, since bindings live for one resolution only (ops_board.py comment at :275-282) and the `exiled_with: "self"` selector reads `exiled_by`, which `exile` sets only under `until_leaves`/`link`, a flag that means "return them" rather than "they are still playable". The duration vocabulary the engine already has for other effects -- `until_your_next_turn` on detain/goad/cant_block (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_board.py:1939,1996) -- proves the clock is representable; it simply has never been wired to the impulse permission. Note the first printed line, "Spectacle {R}", is NOT blocked: it is expressible as a card-level `alternative_cost` of {R} whose `condition` is a `cmp` of `{"life_lost_this_turn": "opponent"}` greater than `{"const": 0}`, which the loader accepts (src/automtg/cards/loader.py:1205-1228). Only the impulse duration blocks the card, so no partial answer was written.
